trades.thesis: AMD rose 8.9% as traders rotated out of NVDA after the scandal. But the bill Congress is pushing would block all AI chip exports to China, which hits AMD's China accelerator sales too. The rally ignores that shared risk, and the hawkish Fed adds pressure on high-valuation semis.

The Fed has made its first hike since 2023, and Waller is putting a 50bp December move on the table. Yet the dollar is flat over 5 days, so the widening rate gap hasn't been priced. Falling oil also eases a source of pressure on the dollar's terms of trade without hurting the US rate advantage.

Nvidia has opened an internal investigation into Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and the BBC frames it as a national security issue. That creates real risk of a CEO change and more Washington scrutiny of China chip sales, on top of hawkish rates weighing on long-duration tech.

Hot October jobs data (+165k, unemployment down to 4.1%) pushed December hike odds past 65%, yet TLT is flat over 5 days (+0.1%). Long bonds look under-priced for a hawkish Fed, and a firm CPI print would close that gap.
